title: MT82 Clutch Controls: Find the Hydraulic Path
introduction:
This component-location reference covers the MT82 manual transmission’s clutch controls. Use the table to match the drawing’s callouts to component names. The transparent vehicle view places the system between the pedal area and transmission; the upper-right inset enlarges the pedal-mounted cylinder, while the upper-left inset shows the release-side cylinder inside the transmission housing.

I follow the system as a relay: your foot moves the pedal, the master cylinder converts that movement into hydraulic pressure, and the fluid tubes carry that pressure to the slave cylinder. The slave cylinder operates the release mechanism, with the release bearing transferring movement to the rotating clutch assembly. The pedal gives the instruction; hydraulics carry the message.

Notice how the pedal and master cylinder sit together while the slave cylinder is at the transmission. That physical separation helps explain why pedal behavior and clutch release belong to the same hydraulic chain. Air or a leak can change pedal feel and release travel even when the friction disc is sound; this drawing alone cannot identify which fault is present.

Use this page to identify and locate the controls before choosing the applicable service or diagnostic procedure. It provides no bleeding sequence, removal route, fluid specification or test limits.
